Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 1 998 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FORCEPS, STAPEDECTOMY, ROUND CUP, 
ELONGATED CUP AND OVAL CUP JAWS 



1. Scope — The dimensions and other requirements for round cup jaw, elongated cup jaw and oval 
cup jaw stapedectomy forceps used in ENT microsurgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 and 1A. 

2.1 The tolerance on various dimensions shall be permitted as given below: 

± 0*05 mm on dimensions up to 5 mm, and 

±0*1 mm on dimensions above 5 mm and up to 10 mm. 

2.2 Joint— As specified in 6 of Section 2 of IS : 3642-1978' General requirements for surgical 
instruments ( first revision ) ' the joint shall be rivetted. 

2.3 Finger Loops — Finger loops shall conform to size 1 of section 5 of IS : 3642-1978, 

3. Materiel — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 30CM3 of IS : 6603-1972 'Specification 
for stainless steel bars and flats \ 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The surfaces of the forceps shall be free from burrs, pits, cracks and other defects. 

4.2 All the edges shall be smoothly rounded and the edges of the cups shall be sharp. 

4.3 The upper jaw shall move freely and smoothly. 

4.4 The cups of the jaws shall register accurately and shall close compfetely without any gap when 
the forceps is closed. 

4.5 The forceps shall be matt finished and passivated. 

4.6 The maximum opening of the upper jaw shall correspond to the maximum opening of the finger 
loops, that is, when the finger loops are opened to their maximum position the jaws shall not move 
further. 

4.7 The jaws shall engage accurately in closed position. 

5. Heat Treatment — The forceps shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 450 to 550 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 The working ends of the forceps shall be tested by picking up at the tip fine hairs or bits of 
threads on the polished surface, for example, a glass surface. 

6.2 Performance — The jaws of the forceps shall be made to bite a double layer of wet blotting 
paper. The jaws shall have a clear impression of the complete sharp edge on the blotting paper They 
shall also be tested on 1 mm thick, natural rubber sheet and the finger loops approximated by a 
force oi about 10 N ( 1 kgf approx ). On release, the forceps shall not show any sign of damage or 
the upper jaw shall not become loose. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance — The forceps shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test as specif led 
in IS:: 7531-1975 ' Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel 
surgical instruments \ 

7. Marking — The forceps shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized 
trade- mark. 

7.1 tSt Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The forceps shall be wrapped in moisture proof paper or packed in polyethylene bag, 
avoiding contact wrth one another. They may also be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier. 



Adopted 27 June 1980 



INDIAN STANDARDS INSTITUTION
